page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured with 12 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM. Powered by the AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture, the system allocates 12 physical cores with one thread per core on a shared CPU model. The server features two NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM. It operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core operations, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier efficiency in text generation for small language models, achieving 349.81 tokens per second.

Given the inclusion of dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs alongside a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per vCPU, this server offers a specialized hardware profile for accelerated compute tasks. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as low-latency LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, data science tasks, and GPU-accelerated rendering or simulation.
